name: space-based
context: High-concurrency distributed systems requiring extreme throughput and low-latency data access through in-memory data grids and distributed processing
benefits: Linear scalability through horizontal partition replication
Sub-millisecond latency with in-memory data access
Elastic capacity to handle traffic spikes dynamically
No single point of failure through partition redundancy
High throughput via parallel processing across nodes
Graceful degradation under peak load conditions
tradeoffs: Eventual consistency between grid and cold storage
Higher infrastructure cost for in-memory storage
Complex debugging and monitoring of distributed state
use_cases: Traffic spikes requiring elastic node scaling
avoid_when: Strong consistency is a hard requirement
Complex relational queries dominate the workload
Small teams with limited distributed systems experience
Simple request-response patterns with no concurrency
Data exceeds available memory across cluster
component_types: Processing Unit: Stateless computation unit containing business logic; scales dynamically based on load
In-Memory Data Grid (Space): Distributed cache partitioned across nodes; provides in-memory data access with replication
Virtual Shared Memory: Logical view of partitioned data providing unified address space across cluster
Messaging Grid: Asynchronous communication layer for inter-component coordination
Deployment Manager: Monitors response times and scales processing units up/down based on demand
Data Pump: Asynchronously synchronizes data between the grid and persistent storage
Space-Based Router: Load balancer that routes requests to appropriate processing units
anti_patterns: Poor partitioning key selection causing data skew
Ignoring network latency in cross-partition operations
Assuming strong consistency across distributed cache
Synchronous database writes blocking the hot path
Cross-partition operations on the critical path
Insufficient testing under realistic load conditions
design_principles: Data Locality: Co-locate processing logic with data partitions to minimize network hops
Partitioning for Access Patterns: Select partition keys that maximize data locality and minimize cross-partition operations
Eventual Consistency: Accept that the grid and cold storage may be temporarily inconsistent; design for reconciliation
Stateless Processing Units: Keep business state in the grid so units can scale and relocate freely
Asynchronous Write-Behind: Persist changes asynchronously via Data Pump; never block the hot path for database writes
One Writer Per Partition: Avoid concurrent writes to same partition; use saga-like patterns for cross-partition work
Replication for Resilience: Maintain backup partitions for automatic failover; test failover regularly
Back-Pressure and Admission Control: Use bounded queues and rate limits to prevent meltdowns during traffic spikes
best_practices: Partition Key Selection: Choose keys that follow access patterns to maximize data locality and minimize cross-shard operations
Replica Strategy: Balance RPO/RTO requirements with cost; test failover and rebalancing regularly against SLOs
Memory Sizing: Carefully size partitions to fit in RAM; monitor memory usage and archive historical data
Observability: Monitor partition distribution, replica health, tail latencies, and grid hit ratios; alert on skew and backlog
Chaos Engineering: Run regular chaos drills for node loss scenarios to validate resilience
Cold Start Handling: Pre-warm the grid by loading hot data from persistent storage before going live
Write Ordering: For critical data, consider synchronous replication to backups to prevent data loss on primary failure
